judgment_calls: Heading-metadata nodes: each section heading's authority tag (developer/user/root) is its own node, and every rule in that section needs it. This follows the heading-metadata rule; the alternative of folding authority into each rule node would duplicate the same claim many times.

The two regulated-advice examples (investment, medical) are separate nodes because each demonstrates the rule with distinct content; the mental-health examples are likewise separate. The alternative of one node per example-pair would merge distinct demonstrations.

The privileged-information section's long paragraphs were split into individual claims (e.g., the four assessment factors, the provenance-metadata rule, the uncertainty rule) rather than one node per paragraph, because each is independently checkable.
The analogy at L1805 is a single node (a fact/illustration), not decomposed into its parts, because it is one explanatory analogy.
The worked examples are each one node covering the whole example block, including the GOOD/BAD comparison, because the dialog inside is not decomposed per the rules.
The commentary blocks (L1712-1713, L1811-1812, L1816-1817) are each one node, as they are commentary/facts, not rules.
The 'uncovered' entries are all blank lines; no content line establishes nothing.
The cross-reference [^...] footnotes are not quoted; quotes were chosen to stop before them or omitted where the reference interrupts the text.
